newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Higher Hungarian beet weight will not boost yield.
newsitem.headline: Higher Hungarian beet weight will not boost yield.

text.p: Hungary said on Friday a higher beet weight in its fourth sugar beet test would not substantially increase its crop in this campaign.
Figures earlier on Friday showed the average root weight was 824 grammes in the fourth test, up from 591 grammes at the smae stage last year.

"The roots were fattened by rains, but their sugar content is very low," Andras Angeli, Chairman of the Sugar Industry Association told Reuters. "Sugar yield per hectare will not be a great deal larger," he added.
Sugar content per beet was 13.5 percent, down from 15 percent in the last campaign.
However, three weeks of sunshine could substantially increase the crop, Angeli added.
But next week's weather in Hungary is likely to be mostly rainy, and a few days of continuous sunshine is only forecast for mid-October, a National Meteorology Service official told Reuters.

Angeli said Hungary planned to produce 460,000 tonnes of sugar in this campaign, down from 480,000 tonnes in the last one, but sugar beet exports were likely to reach 500,000 tonnes, up from 370,000 tonnes.
Domestic factories would probably produce sugar from 3.8 million tonnes of beets in this campaign, compared with four million tonnes in the last campaign, Angeli added.
